summary_hint: passport for <full_name>, nationality <nationality_or_citizenship>, passport no. <document_number>, issued <issue_date> (<place_of_issue>) expiring <expiry_date> — so a processor can confirm identity and that the travel document is unexpired.

typed_core.name: document_type_as_printed
typed_core.why: identity — the card genre as printed (passport / permanent resident / employment authorization / state ID)

typed_core.name: surname
typed_core.why: identity — family name as printed

typed_core.name: given_names
typed_core.why: identity — given/first + middle names as printed

typed_core.name: full_name
typed_core.why: identity — the individual; attaches to the borrower for ID-1 name matching

typed_core.name: date_of_birth
typed_core.why: PII (highly_restricted) + identity — disambiguates same-named individuals; unmasked (ID-3 matches on it)

typed_core.name: document_number
typed_core.why: PII (highly_restricted) + identity — the primary front number (passport no / card # / ID #)

typed_core.name: uscis_or_a_number
typed_core.why: PII (highly_restricted) — the USCIS#/A-Number on a green card or EAD; identity/linkage
typed_core.prompt_hint: USCIS#/A-Number/Alien Reg. No. (8-9 digits, often NNN-NNN-NNN) — NOT the card number

typed_core.name: issue_date
typed_core.why: processor — when the document was issued (passport/ID); null on a green card

typed_core.name: expiry_date
typed_core.why: processor — headline: is the document unexpired through closing ('Date of Expiry'/'Card Expires')

typed_core.name: valid_from_date
typed_core.why: processor — an EAD's 'Valid From'; null elsewhere

typed_core.name: resident_since_date
typed_core.why: processor — a green card's 'Resident Since'; null elsewhere

typed_core.name: category_code
typed_core.why: processor — immigration category verbatim (EAD 'C26', green card 'E26'); null on passport/ID
typed_core.pii: capture the code verbatim (e.g. C26, E26) beside 'Category'

typed_core.name: employment_terms_or_restriction
typed_core.why: processor — an EAD's Terms & Conditions / restriction line (e.g. 'None', 'NOT VALID FOR REENTRY')

typed_core.name: issuing_country_or_state
typed_core.why: processor — issuing country (passport) or issuing US state (state ID)

typed_core.name: issuing_authority
typed_core.why: processor — the issuing office/authority (passport office, USCIS, a state DMV)

typed_core.name: place_or_country_of_birth
typed_core.why: processor — 'Place of Birth' (passport/ID) or 'Country of Birth' (green card/EAD)

typed_core.name: nationality_or_citizenship
typed_core.why: processor — nationality as printed (passports print this)

typed_core.name: place_of_issue
typed_core.why: processor — a passport's 'Place of Issue' (city); null elsewhere

typed_core.name: government_id_type
typed_core.why: identity — for a generic ID, the kind (State ID / National ID); null for passport/green-card/EAD

typed_core.name: residential_address
typed_core.why: processor — a residential address if the document prints one

rejected.name: sex
rejected.reason: OPTIONAL; no mortgage consumer and adds protected-class exposure — dropped from the shared core (LP-472, aligning to spec 108's rejection)

rejected.name: machine_readable_zone (MRZ)
rejected.reason: re-encodes name/DOB/number/expiry already typed, and its contiguous digit run trips the at-rest _LONG_DIGITS guard; captured in the catch-all if read (LP-472)

rejected.name: photo_present / signature_present
rejected.reason: no mortgage consumer; a card always has them

rejected.name: receipt_number / i94_admission_number / visa_number / passport_number (as a separate field)
rejected.reason: not printed on the identity card itself (they belong to the I-797/visa foil); the catch-all captures any that appear

encoding_variations: The four kinds share ONE field set (LP-472); a given card fills only its printed fields and nulls the rest.
Expiry is 'Date of Expiry' (passport), 'Card Expires' (green card / EAD), or 'Expiration' (ID) — all map to expiry_date.
A green card shows 'Resident Since' and no issue date; an EAD shows 'Valid From' — these are distinct date fields, not issue_date.
USCIS#/A-Number (green card / EAD) is distinct from the card's front number — keep the A-number in uscis_or_a_number, the card number in document_number.
notes: LP-472: passport was the one family type with NO extractor (Tier-2). Promoted to Tier-1 on the shared identity core; extracts via the shared extract_identity_document. Typed_core IDENTICAL across the family (drift-locked by test).
A passport is a travel/re-entry document; the MRZ, place_of_issue and back-page fields (father/mother/spouse, file no, prior passport) are captured (MRZ + kin in the catch-all).
nationality_or_citizenship and place_of_issue are passport-populated; category_code/valid_from_date/resident_since_date/government_id_type stay null.
